title: Prove native F2 innovation beyond the earlier centre history
body:
I prove that a decoder cannot recover the selected F2 query from the complete centre history of calls 0..9 alone. I construct coupled source/target differences for which all 80 earlier fields vanish across all owners, while the eight F2 fields at one owner range over the full payload space.

The conditional theorem is `Q(ker H) = M^8`. Even with arbitrary decoding, a linear fresh observation needs at least `8 dim(M)` complex coordinates to recover that query. I use the retained native common-frame and full-space cover-view hypotheses and verify the selected chronological premises. I infer no recursive-child count or supplier saving.

I credit David Charbonneau's PR3147 for the circle proposal, Nick Petalas's PR3151 for the full-input scalar warning, Aaron Wang/navinor and ywz65 for kernel/owner-route arguments, DLamdata for native endpoint gauges, and the selected native construction lineage. The new scope includes all earlier centre fields and varying original targets; it differs from the source-only terminal factorization and scalar rank16 audit.

I passed the registered Python 3.12 replay with `-I -O -B`: both complete scalar endpoints, 16 reverse-derived cuts, the 19-event prefix, 112 routes, 1,344 native boundary identities, 112 kernel vectors, six algebraic controls and three premise mutations. The response determinant is `52^8 × 32`. I also passed metadata/source-pin and commit-byte validation. I confirmed that GitHub's [plan and package replay](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39049866864) passed for head `080309ba9e29449ea4f29971e0ce1d9278703350`.

Reproduce with:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-history-innovation
```

I leave native compiler admission, fixed-grid realization, fresh-data acquisition, cache restoration and the full supplier invoice open. I keep the selected frontier unchanged. I contribute as `jmbarrancoml` with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; I claim no independent human or formal-kernel verification.

Coordination and handoff: [Discussion #3149](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3149#discussioncomment-19000929).
